basis: Consolidated, Rs Crore unless noted. All rows sourced from https://www.screener.in/company/PCJEWELLER/consolidated/ (Profit & Loss / Balance Sheet / Ratios / Cash Flow tables, fetched 2026-09-24).
shares_outstanding_note: Back-solved as Net Profit / EPS per year (both from the same table, so internally consistent): ~357cr shares FY15-FY17, ~394cr shares FY18 onward (jump consistent with the 2017 1:1 bonus plus an additional capital raise -- see corp_actions/pcjeweller.json). Equity Capital in the BS table is on the as-filed, non-split-adjusted basis and should NOT be used directly for a current per-share count.
capex_proxy_caveat: Screener's free tables do not expose a discrete 'capital expenditure' line; 'capex_proxy_cr' below is the year's 'Cash from Investing Activity' total (includes capex, asset sales, investment purchases/sales netted together) as the nearest available proxy. It is NOT a clean capex figure -- a schedule-level breakdown (via Screener's expandable 'Fixed Assets +' / investing-activity sub-items) was not retrieved (no working API endpoint found for it in the time available). Depreciation is exact (P&L line item).
net_debt_proxy_caveat: Cash & bank balances are folded into the BS table's 'Other Assets +' aggregate and not broken out separately at this fetch depth. 'net_debt_proxy_cr' below uses gross Borrowings only (i.e. likely OVERSTATES true net debt by the amount of cash/investments held). 'Investments' row (a separate, smaller BS line, likely non-cash financial investments) is given separately where present.

FY2019.note: PAT ~zero; CFO deeply negative (-1931cr) despite reported operating profit -- classic red flag (profit not converting to cash, consistent with receivables-quality allegations).

beta: not sourced -- no reliable point-in-time (FY2016-2018) beta was located; current(2026)-only beta figures from third-party sites were not used because they postdate the scoring dates by 8-10 years and this company's risk profile changed enormously across that span (pre- vs post-collapse), making a current beta meaningless as a PIT DCF input.
forensic_flags_visible_as_of_scoring_dat: As of 2017-03-31 (FY17 just-reported): Debtor Days had already risen from 45 (FY15) to 66 (FY17), a 47% increase against 33% revenue growth over the same period -- receivables growing faster than sales, a classic early red flag, visible in the data at the scoring date to anyone who pulled the ratios table.

As of 2018-03-31 (FY18 just-reported): Debtor Days 70, Inventory Days 232 -- both still elevated but not yet extreme; FY18 was the last 'normal-looking' reported year (PAT Rs 536cr, EPS growth intact) before the FY19 collapse. A DCF/anchor entry AT this date would not yet see the eventual near-total PAT wipeout in the reported numbers themselves, only the receivables-days drift noted above.

OPM (EBITDA margin) held a stable 9-11% band FY15-18, only collapsing to 3.4% in FY19 -- margin compression was NOT a leading indicator ahead of the two scored dates; the leading indicator (to the extent one existed in the numbers) was working-capital quality (debtor/inventory days), not profitability.
